harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Published node2's HTTP service (port 8080) on node1's management address (10.100.205.10) port 80 using OPNsense NAT: a source-scoped rdr (port-forward) rule restricted to node3 (10.100.205.12), a matching hybrid-mode outbound SNAT rule (rewriting source to node1's LAN IP so node2's flat-L2 replies route back through node1), and an explicit reject filter rule that returns a deterministic TCP RST ("connection refused") for any other source hitting port 80. Also had to stand up the node2 HTTP service itself (busybox httpd via OpenRC, was not pre-existing) and disable OPNsense's built-in port-80 HTTPS-redirect listener/protection which was intercepting port 80 before the NAT rule could apply. Verified end-to-end from node3 (succeeds) and node2/node1-self (refused) both before and after restarting all three nodes one at a time with proof of changed boot identity and post-restart recovery.
actions_performed: Surveyed node1 (OPNsense/FreeBSD), node2 (Alpine), node3 (Alpine) network/service state
Installed busybox-extras and configured an OpenRC-managed busybox httpd on node2:8080 serving 'hello from node2:8080'

Edited /conf/config.xml on node1: added NAT port-forward (rdr) rule interface=lan tcp dst=10.100.205.10:80 -> target 10.100.205.11:8080, source restricted to 10.100.205.12/32 (node3), associated-rule-id=pass
Discovered and disabled OPNsense's default http->https webgui redirect (system/webgui/disablehttpredirect=1) which was shadowing port 80 via built-in 'no rdr ... port=http' protection

Discovered flat L2 topology caused asymmetric routing (node2 replying directly to node3, bypassing node1); fixed by switching outbound NAT to hybrid mode and adding an SNAT rule so forwarded traffic to node2:8080 is source-translated to node1's LAN IP
Added an explicit pf reject filter rule (block return) for tcp/80 to node1's LAN IP from any source except node3, ensuring deterministic 'Connection refused' for all other sources
Ran configctl filter reload after each config.xml change and verified via pfctl -s nat / pfctl -s rules
Verified via curl from node3 (success, 200 OK with body), node2 (connection refused), and node1 itself (connection refused)
Captured baseline boot identity (kern.boottime for node1, /proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id for node2/node3) and health for all three nodes
Restarted node1, node2, node3 sequentially (one at a time) via native reboot commands backgrounded so the ack returned before disconnect; polled each until exec access returned

Confirmed changed boot identity for each node post-restart and re-verified functional recovery (NAT/filter rules persisted on node1 via config.xml, mini-http service auto-started via OpenRC on node2, end-to-end curl test from node3 succeeded, node2 still refused) after each restart

evidence.requirement: node2 HTTP service on 8080 exists and is healthy (baseline + post-restart)
evidence.summary: busybox httpd installed and started on node2:8080 via OpenRC (mini-http), confirmed listening and serving content both before and after node2's restart (new boot_id 0869979b... vs baseline 7954d12c...)

evidence.requirement: Port 80 on node1's management address (10.100.205.10) is published and forwards to node2:8080, reachable by node3
evidence.summary: Added NAT rdr rule (source-restricted to node3) plus a hybrid-mode outbound SNAT rule to fix asymmetric L2 return routing; node3's curl to 10.100.205.10:80 returns HTTP 200 with node2's body 'hello from node2:8080'

evidence.requirement: Published port stays refused for every other source address (node2 itself, node1 itself)
evidence.summary: Added explicit pf reject (block return, sends RST) filter rule for tcp/80 to node1's LAN IP excluding source 10.100.205.12; verified node2 and node1-self both get deterministic 'Connection refused'

evidence.requirement: node1 mandatory restart: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline kern.boottime=1788626410 (16:40:10); reboot acknowledged and returned before disconnect; post-restart kern.boottime=1788626851 (16:47:31, changed); NAT/filter rules persisted from config.xml and functional test (node3 success, node2 refused) confirmed recovery

evidence.requirement: node2 mandatory restart: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 7954d12c-8957-4a50-8edc-443719e4654f; reboot acknowledged and returned before disconnect; post-restart boot_id 0869979b-d6c3-437b-81fa-8917da53e045 (changed); mini-http auto-started via OpenRC and end-to-end curl from node3 succeeded

evidence.requirement: node3 mandatory restart: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 89dc5330-c3f6-4be9-8663-023b27d7cf7b; reboot acknowledged and returned before disconnect; post-restart boot_id 5a3d72d2-3951-436d-87b7-0aef755aafed (changed); final verification confirms node3 still reaches published service and node2 remains refused
